title: Mission: drive motor gear ratio via forward/backward sonar ranging
description: Determine the drive-train calibration: drive the robot forward/backward to the same spot (encoder-driven legs) and read the displacement from the chassis-mounted sonar (obstacle 75 cm dead-ahead = position oracle). Yields ticks/cm of travel (the odometry constant bundling gear ratio + track sprocket diameter), the forward/backward asymmetry (drivetrain backlash/slip), and the left/right symmetry. Kinect depth cross-checks the distances. The true motor:sprocket ratio needs the sprocket diameter measured separately.
notes: 2026-10-25: the rear track BROKE mid-run (all run-1 data invalid, retracted). Valid findings: the drive train is geared ~6x deeper than the turret (~1.16 ticks/s per speed unit vs 7.2 - the legs must budget at the drive rate); the sonar is blind WHILE the tracks turn (EMI/vibration) and only works at rest; the kinect depth works during motion but the USB storms gap it. After the repair + repositioning the obstacle is at 43 cm (sonar) / 0.50 m (kinect) - too close for 15 cm excursions. BLOCKED on the user repositioning the robot to ~75-80 cm with >=40 cm clear behind.

Mission: 90-degree turret swing reliability (encoder/color/kinect)
description: Test whether the turret can reliably swing +/-90 deg off center and return: cable limits and stall behavior, encoder drift/backlash over large excursions, the color fingerprint beyond the mapped range, kinect scene verification. Robot static. Sensors: encoder (PORT_C), color (PORT_1), sonar (PORT_4, 75 cm obstacle ground truth), kinect depth. Ratio caveat: 125 ticks/deg is +-10 percent, so legs are encoder-driven (stop on reached ticks), not time-driven.
notes:
2026-10-25 mission complete: +90/-180/+90 encoder-driven legs all 100% of target, no stalls, no cable limits in the +-90 span; return error 6 ticks (0.05 deg) after fixing the command-queue backlog (stream at the 0.3 s consumption rate). Color fingerprint reproduced exactly (768->768) and spans 734-768 across +-90 deg; sonar 75 cm constant; kinect blob re-centered (x=335). Raw: doc/sources/2026-10-25-swing90-run.md
2026-10-25 repeat run: trajectory repeats within +-10 ticks after start-offset alignment; color reproduces within 1-2 counts at every pose; return 91 ticks (vs 6) - honest bound +-100 ticks (±0.8 deg), set by the recenter. Both runs fit blob_x = 320 + (enc-401)*0.092 -> TRUE CENTER = encoder ~+401 (the backlash midpoint); blob hysteresis ~12-15 px between approaches. The per-frame ratio cross-check failed on encoder timestamp skew - interpolate the encoder at frame times next time; 125 ticks/deg stands on the optical method.

title: Turret homing via color sensor index (cable at camera-forward)
description: Homing: swing toward center watching PORT_1 color; stop on sustained deviation; record encoder = forward reference; track absolute turret angle via encoder + 125 ticks/deg (measured). OPEN: first detected feature (enc -3468) does not match expected cable position - identify landmarks by re-crossing at the same encoder value. Turret travel is cable-limited - never rotate unbounded. Evidence: doc/sources/2026-10-25-turret-calibration.md
notes:
2026-10-25 homing run: obstacle (sonar 75 cm dead-ahead) centered on the Kinect at encoder +527, color ~790 at center (gradient fingerprint, not a step). Sonar never changes with turret angle (chassis-fixed) - it is the distance oracle. Ratio discrepancy (125 far-scene vs ~165-198 near-field implied) = parallax; 125 stands pending a distant-target measurement. Turret now ~6 deg left of center (enc +1268). fd-leak fix deployed (get_voltage SMBus close) - was the true telemetry-death root cause.
2026-10-25 centering run: landmark REPRODUCES but depends on approach direction - left approach centered at enc +527, right approach at +271-275: gear backlash ~252 ticks (~2 deg at 125 ticks/deg). V2 homing must approach from one direction or model the backlash. Tilt -8.5deg moved the obstacle depth reading from 0.79m to 0.70m (sonar 75cm) - down-tilt improves distance agreement.

title: Decide v2 perception accelerator (NCS1 vs CPU-first vs other USB)
description: Robot has an Intel NCS1 in boot mode with a dead archived SDK; Coral EOL 2026; Hailo needs PCIe (RPi 3 lacks it). Recommendation: CPU INT8 inference as default backend, NCS1 as experimental option (mirror'd NCSDK per ncs-legacy-support.md), keep inference behind a backend interface. Decide before vision Phase 5. title: camerad: Rust Kinect capture daemon (libfreenect FFI, throttled)
description: Replace unthrottled KinectProcess: libfreenect C API via FFI (callback + process_events_timeout, latest-frame-wins), throttled to 10-15 fps, frames only for client stream / features for control. Start from external/libfreenect-rs + regen libfreenect-sys. Fixes koc-hw-kinect-wedge. API surface: doc/architecture/kinect-interface.md

title: motord: Rust BrickPi+ UART driver prototype (protocol parity vs BrickPi.py)
description: Implement the BrickPi+ protocol in Rust over serialport-rs: 500kbaud /dev/ttyS0, framing [dest][checksum][count][payload] (tx) / [checksum][count][payload] (rx), two ATmega destinations (1,2), MSG_TYPE VALUES/E_STOP/TIMEOUT_SETTINGS. Enable the firmware deadman (TIMEOUT_SETTINGS), wire E_STOP to crash handlers, port the US-sensor I2C workaround. Validate with differential tests vs BrickPi.py on the robot. Protocol: doc/architecture/brickpi-interface.md
notes: 2026-10-25 finding from koc-swing90: the v1 100-deep command queue backs up during streaming (10 Hz in, ~3.3/s consumed) and keeps executing after stop - a 1641-tick (13 deg) overshoot. V2 motord must drop stale commands (timestamped, bounded queue) - matches microduck's deadman doctrine.

Also missing excludes for .beads/ (embedded Dolt DB), .claude/, external/ (146 MB of reference clones). Fix: explicit target dir name + extend exclude list. title: Kinect capture wedge: unthrottled loop + fork-inherited ZMQ fds stall server telemetry
description: KinectProcess (multiprocessing fork) is started after the parent server has created its ZMQ context/sockets, so the child inherits copies of them (visible in ss output: child owns fds on :5557). The capture loop is also unthrottled: 5.7 GB pushed to the aggregator in 33 min at 139% CPU. After some minutes the aggregator stops publishing (360 KB stranded unread in its TCP recv buffer) and BrickPiWrapper stops sending, with no Python errors logged. Restarting server.py recovers. Kinect also sits behind two USB hubs causing libfreenect resync storms (log spam, likely contributes). Fix: throttle capture loop (sleep to ~10-15 fps), fork Kinect before creating parent ZMQ sockets or use spawn, move Kinect to a dedicated USB port. Evidence: doc/sources/2026-10-24-robot-state-capture.md
notes:
2026-10-25: spawn context + 10 fps throttle deployed (app/server/kinect_process.py rewritten). New findings: orphaned spawn children survive restarts (SIGTERM does not reap daemon children - restart must also pkill multiprocessing.spawn); the Kinect USB link via the two-hub chain enters chronic resync storms (Stream 70) within minutes of streaming, spinning the child at ~135% and jamming the aggregator (5557 fills to HWM, telemetry dies). Physical fix required: Kinect on a dedicated USB port. Watcher logging endurance at /tmp/koc_stream_watch.log on the robot.
2026-10-25 constraint from user: the Kinect MUST stay on the hub chain - it provides power the RPi3 port cannot supply (direct port not an option). Root cause refined: two hub hops in series + ~25 MB/s constant wire load on the shared 480 Mbps root bus + power sharing. Mitigation options: single quality powered hub; demand-driven capture in v2 camerad; self-healing worker for v1.
Self-healing deployed and validated: watchdog exits the child on 10s frame stall, reaper respawns in <=3s (kill test passed); SIGTERM handler prevents orphan children. Chronic Storm-70 degradation still expected on the hub chain - recovery now costs seconds, not the server.
SECOND root cause found+fixed 2026-10-25: get_voltage() leaked one SMBus fd per call -> Too many open files killed the BrickPiWrapper thread in ~15-20 min -> telemetry gone. Fixed with a with-block (closed per read); deployed.
